links.outcome: Cross-dataset generalization drop in landmark error versus in-domain performance
links.effect: In-domain MRE 2.47-3.04 mm (Aariz) and 4.12-5.55 mm (ISBI); cross-dataset error rose 155-426%; single-dataset accuracy substantially overstates clinical generalizability.
links.quote: Single-dataset accuracy substantially overstates clinical generalizability, and the best in-domain architecture is not the most transferable, so in-domain leaderboards are an unreliable basis for selecting a model for clinical deployment; balanced multi-source training recovers most of the loss across the architectures tested.

links.outcome: Device-specific performance shift under leave-one-device-out evaluation
links.effect: Leave-one-device-out revealed reproducible device-specific shift with held-out MRE 1.89-7.94 mm.
links.quote: Leave-one-device-out revealed reproducible device-specific shift (held-out MRE 1.89-7.94 mm).

links.outcome: Performance degradation when test data differ from development data
links.effect: Cross-domain errors were 15-44x the 0.53 mm inter-observer band; Generalization Drop 155-426%; A-point, B-point, Nasion, Menton exceeded 2 mm threshold out-of-domain.
links.quote: A-point, B-point, Nasion, and Menton all exceeded the 2 mm clinical threshold out-of-domain, including points localized to sub-millimeter accuracy in-domain.

links.outcome: Effect of balanced multi-source joint training on cross-domain error gap
links.effect: Balanced joint training reduced the cross-domain gap for all four architectures (both domains about 2.1-3.5 mm) without harming in-domain accuracy.
links.quote: Balanced joint training reduced the cross-domain gap for all four architectures (both domains ≈ 2.1-3.5 mm) without harming in-domain accuracy.

links.outcome: Whether in-domain ranking of architectures predicts cross-domain ranking
links.effect: Best in-domain model (from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop; in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.
links.quote: The most accurate model in-domain (a from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop, and every pretrained estimate fell below every from-scratch estimate (family means 248% vs. 380%): in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.

unlisted_practices: Pretraining on large datasets to improve cross-domain transfer (mixed: halved error Aariz to ISBI, 7.73 vs 16.36 mm, but not in reverse)

screen.reason: The study empirically tests how in-domain benchmarking fails to generalize across different clinical devices/datasets for cephalometric landmark detection, and evaluates multi-source training and pretraining strategies to mitigate cross-device/domain generalization drops before clinical deployment.

primary.practice: multi-source balanced joint training and external cross-domain validation
